newsitem.title: KENYA: Border raid reported despite Ethiopia, Kenya pact.
newsitem.headline: Border raid reported despite Ethiopia, Kenya pact.

text.p: An agreement between Ethiopia and Kenya to end border conflict was dealt a blow by a report on Saturday that 24 Kenyan tribesmen had been killed after a cross border raid.
Ethiopian state television said on Friday night Ethiopian and Kenyan officials in the southern Ethiopian town of Awassa had signed an agreement to end clan clashes along their borders.
It said officials were trying to resolve differences between Ethiopia's Geleb tribe and the Turkana of Kenya. A joint border commission would meet in August to review progress on keeping peace.
But on Saturday Kenya's independent Daily Nation newspaper said 24 Turkana raiders were killed in northern Kenya last Monday after attacking Ethiopian Merrile cattle herders across the border.

It said Turkana tribesmen attacked a Merrile camp near the border, killing women and children, and stole hundreds of cattle and were pursued back into Kenya by Merrile fighters who battled with them for six hours and recaptured some of their animals.
The newspaper quoted a senior police officer in the region and said the number of Ethiopian dead was unknown. A spokesman at police headquarters in Nairobi was not available to comment.

More than 80 Kenyans, including 17 policemen, were killed on March 23 when Ethiopian clan raiders attacked Turkana camps, the Nation said. Cattle rustling and killings in the usually arid border region are common with attackers using automatic weapons.
